prompt:
Reddit post, r/houseplants.
Title: Heeeey reddit wtf is that and why isn't alcohol working?

This was my very first syngonium. I absolutely will. Not. Lose. It. It started my love for syngoniums and i just cannot lose it. I have sprayed this thing down so many times in the last few weeks. I've used peroxide, alcohol, insecticide, neem, I tried fungicide as a last ditch! What is is and how to I make them disappear!?

I've had a nasty mealy problem for the last year ish but haven't lost a plant yet. These didn't look like mealies to I wasn't too sure what to do and everything either reeks and isn't working or smells slightly better and still isn't working.

What is wrong with my plant?
answer:
This looks like **mealybugs**. The white, waxy, cottony specks along the stems, leaf bases, and leaf surfaces are typical, and the sticky sheen points the same way. The brown, crispy leaves are likely damage from the repeated alcohol and peroxide sprays combined with pest feeding. Sprays only hit exposed surfaces, while mealybugs hide in leaf joints and stem nodes, which is why nothing seems to work. Dead leaves won't recover, but new growth should stay clean once the pests are gone.

1. **Stop spraying the whole plant** with alcohol, peroxide, or other sprays. Keep the plant away from your other plants while you treat it.
2. **Remove the mostly brown leaves** with clean scissors and bag them. Keep any green leaves.
3. **Dab each visible mealybug** with a cotton swab dipped in 70% isopropyl alcohol, focusing on leaf bases, stem joints, and leaf undersides. Repeat every 3 days for 3 weeks, about 10 minutes each time.
4. **Check the roots.** Slide the plant out of its pot. If you see white cottony masses on the roots, rinse them off under lukewarm water and repot in fresh mix. If the roots are clean, skip this.

Once the swabbing is done, you can also spray the whole plant weekly with insecticidal soap (such as Safer Brand, mixed per the label, about $10) to catch any survivors. Coat the undersides too, and let it dry before moving the plant.
